chunks: From him, from Ibrahim, from al-Barqi, from Sulayman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari, from Musa ibn Hamzah ibn Bazi', who said:

I said to Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام: May I be made your ransom, I have an estate short of Baghdad. I set out from al-Kufah intending Baghdad, and I stay in that estate. Should I shorten or complete? He said: If you do not intend to stay for ten days, then shorten.

And the second possibility is that the reports are to be understood as applying to one who passes by a residence of his that he had made his homeland for six months or more; at that point, completing the prayer becomes obligatory upon him. That is indicated by what follows.

key_terms.أُتِمُّ: I complete the prayer in full
key_terms.أُقَصِّرُ: I shorten the prayer during travel
key_terms.اسْتَوْطَنَهُ: he had adopted it as a place of residence
key_terms.التَّمَامُ: performing the prayer in full rather than shortened
key_terms.الْمُقَامَ: intended residence or staying in a place
key_terms.ضَيْعَةً: an estate or landed property where one stays
key_terms.عَشَرَةَ أَيَّامٍ: the legal period of ten days affecting the travel ruling

ai.seo_question: When must a traveler shorten or complete salat (prayer) at his own estate according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling of salat (prayer) for a traveler who stops at his estate on the way to Baghdad. The Imam عليه السلام rules that if he does not intend to reside for ten days, he should shorten the prayer, while the concluding juristic note explains that completion applies in the case of a place established as a residence for six months or more.
